Inductors can either be fixed or variable and are normally referred to as coils or chokes. The term "choke" is commonly used for inductors whose application is radio frequency.
The amount of induced voltage produced by an inductor depends on several factors: Permeability of core material Core cross-sectional area Core length Number of turns
The core is made from a variety of materials, commonly a ferromagnetic compound, iron or air.
An inductor consists of a length of wire coiled around a given medium called the core.
Inductance refers to the ability of a conductor to create an induced voltage when current flow through the conductor is varied; such as AC or varying DC.
Through earlier studies of inductors, you have learned about their electrical properties and the effects that they have in circuits. However, a quick review of inductor basics is appropriate.

The time required by an RL circuit to rise to maximum current or drop to zero current is based upon the values of the inductor(s) and the resistor(s). The more inductive the circuit, the longer the time constant, and vice-versa...
